turns.t: Morning, doctor. I've brought Mrs Adeyemi through from the waiting room. Her daughter's just parking the car, she'll be along in a minute.
Thank you. Good morning, Mrs Adeyemi, do sit down. And you are...?
Joy. I'm her carer, I come in mornings and evenings.
Lovely. So, Mrs Adeyemi, what's brought you in to see me today?
Well, it's... I don't really know that there's, um...
Sorry I'm late, the car park is a nightmare. Has Mum said anything yet? She's been so tired since she came out of hospital in the spring.
I wouldn't say tired, exactly. Just a bit, you know...
A bit what, Mrs Adeyemi? Take your time.
Slow. I'm not tired. Slow, that's all.
Slow is a good word for it. Is it all day, or worse at certain times?
Mornings are fine. It's after lunch that I...
After lunch, you...?
She's asleep in the armchair by three o'clock, every single afternoon. Joy finds her there.
I'm only resting my eyes.
She's eating well, I'll say that for her. I made her a proper dinner yesterday and she cleared the plate.
That's good to hear, appetite is a useful clue. Mrs Adeyemi, how do you feel about the afternoons yourself?
It's only resting, dear. Everybody rests.
They do. Everyone's batteries run down. I'm just wondering whether yours are recharging as well as they used to.
Perhaps not quite...
Fair enough. Do you live on your own, or with family?
On my own. In my flat. The ground floor one, I've been there forty years.
With Joy coming in twice a day, and me most weekends.
That sounds a good set-up. Mrs Adeyemi, would you mind if I had a look at your neck? Just to see how everything has settled.
Oh. Yes, if you like.
Chin up a little for me. Mm. The scar has healed very neatly, it's flat and quite pale now.
That's good, is it?
It's very good. Nice tidy healing, whoever did it knew their stuff.
But what about the sleeping, doctor? That's why I wanted her seen.

Of course. I'll tell you what I think. It looks most likely that she's still catching up after the hospital stay. Picture a phone battery that's had a rough month: it takes a while before it holds its charge like before.
Catching up.
Yes. And that sort of thing tends to improve gradually, not overnight.
So it's not something we should be worried about?
Nothing I've seen today worries me, no.

What helps meanwhile is a short walk in the morning light, a proper lunch, and if she does need the afternoon rest, half an hour on her bed rather than the armchair, so it doesn't swallow the whole afternoon.
I can walk her round the block before lunch, weather permitting. She likes the little park.
I do like the park.
Then that's settled. Joy, if you're happy to keep going as you are, that's all anyone can ask.
Thank you, doctor. I'll stop fussing, I promise.
Thank you, doctor.
Not at all. Off you go, and don't let her skip lunch.
